stories.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
summary: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,116 Palestinians in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian Authority figures.
Palestinian attacks or clashes between Palestinians and Israeli forces have killed at least 51 Israelis during the same period, according to official Israeli figures.

stories.title: Anthropic unveils new Fable, Mythos models as competition heats up ahead of IPO
summary: Anthropic on Monday unveiled two new artificial intelligence models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the OpenAI rival seeks to strengthen its position in the fast-growing AI market ahead of its planned initial public offering (IPO).
The company said Claude Fable 5.2 was designed for coding, reasoning and AI agent tasks, while Claude Mythos 5.2 was developed for approved cybersecurity and life-sciences research applications.

Access to Claude Mythos 5.2 will be restricted to organisations approved through Anthropic’s verification programmes for cybersecurity and life-sciences research, while Claude Fable 5.2 will be available more broadly, the company said.

stories.title: Trump nominates Natalie Baker for US ambassador to Pakistan
summary: US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, the current charge d’affaires at the US embassy in Islamabad, to be the ambassador to Pakistan, according to a statement by the White House.
She had arrived in Islamabad as deputy chief of mission in August 2024, according to details available on the embassy’s website.

Baker was also deployed as the deputy chief of mission and charge d’affaires of the US Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the US consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the US embassy in Kuwait.

stories.title: Saud Shakeel nears century as Pakistan score 390-6 in first Test against Sri Lanka
summary: Saud Shakeel was edging towards a century on Tuesday as Pakistan reached lunch at 390-6 on day two of the opening Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi.
Sri Lanka had hoped for early wickets but on a seemingly hard and green pitch their bowlers struggled despite taking the second new ball after 80 overs.
Pace bowlers Asitha Fernando with 2-87 and Madushanka (2-97) were the pick of the Sri Lanka attack.

stories.title: Trump sets off bedlam in White House briefing room with UFC chief's appearance
summary: President Donald Trump set off a scramble in the White House press briefing room on Monday with an appearance so sudden that aides had no time to place the presidential seal on the podium.
After heavy Republican losses in the midterm elections less than a week ago, Trump announced on Saturday that he had offered the White House press secretary job to White.

Trump said on Sunday he was just teasing, but White came to the White House anyway to see the president. “Everyone please take a seat in the briefing room RIGHT NOW,” was a press assistant’s urgent instruction for reporters over the loudspeaker.

stories.title: Two years in, women leaving top roles in Trump admin
summary: The abrupt exit of White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, one day after Republicans were stomped in midterm elections, adds her to a growing list of women who have departed top roles in President Donald Trump’s administration since the year began.
She was followed by Trump’s top federal prosecutor Pam Bondi, Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer and Tulsi Gabbard, director of national intelligence.
And Wiles — the first woman to hold the strategic position of White House chief of staff — has just been replaced by hard-right ideologue Miller, a longtime Trump loyalist.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz to leave for Turkiye today, will address COP31 tomorrow
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will be undertaking a visit to Antalya in Turkiye from Nov 10-12 to participate in the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP 31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Negotiators had been locked in discussions late on Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation.

Inventor said developed countries were “taking a hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations.

stories.title: Honey Traps: A spy’s oldest trick
summary: The latest controversy to ripple through the tech world centres on Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and his affair with a woman accused by Washington of working for Chinese intelligence, a claim Beijing denies.

The episode has thrust the “honey trap” back into the spotlight, reviving interest in an age-old spying tactic that turns attraction and intimacy into tools for stealing state secrets and influencing those in power.
Another famous case, Renault said, involved the Soviet KGB blackmailing British embassy employee John Vassall with “intimate photos revealing his homosexuality, taken in Moscow”.

stories.title: Fossil fuel emissions fall due to Iran war, renewables: research
summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday.

Emissions from the burning of oil, gas and coal — the main drivers of climate change —rose by 0.9 per cent per year on average in the past decade, hitting a record high in 2025, according to the Global Carbon Budget report.
Oil-related emissions are projected to drop 1.9 percent last year but it was “likely a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict”, the researchers said.

stories.title: Police claim completing probe into anchorperson’s death
summary: RAWALPINDI: The withdrawal of the murder case of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan has nothing to do with the police, as any compromise between the complainant and the suspect can only be decided by the trial court, a senior police officer has said.
Officer says only court can decide on withdrawal of case According to the initial police examination of Rabia’s body, she had sustained a gunshot wound below the neck.
Khuram Ahmed, a resident of Sector G-7/3-4, Islamabad, and brother of the deceased anchorperson, had registered the FIR with Saddar Bairooni police against Rabia’s husband, Muhammad Ahsan.

stories.title: Residents irked by road closure for Sindhi Muslim Food Walk in Karachi
summary: Advocate Aziz said the food walk has been set up by closing a main road to traffic, a move he believes goes against a February 2023 order of the Sindh High Court in a similar case involving the Burns Road Food Street.
The lawyer, who had represented the petitioners in the Burns Road food street case, says the Sindhi Muslim Food Walk runs contrary to the SHC order passed in 2023.
In that case, the court has directed the local administration to end the evening food street set up on a portion of Burns Road and restore the road to vehicular traffic.

The witnesses also said the women referred to an earlier inquiry in a harassment case in which the teacher had reportedly been cleared of the allegations.

Faculty member attacked by two women at a conference Meanwhile, the Old Ravians, a body comprising former students of the institution, expressed concern over what it described as recurring allegations of harassment, bullying, blackmail and extortion against the teacher.

stories.title: Repatriation of illegal Afghan nationals slows down in Khyber
summary: Meanwhile, complaints about the theft or mysterious disappearance of costly personal items belonging to returning Afghans during customs clearance and border crossing have surfaced in recent weeks.

They said that returning Afghans had also complained about the confiscation of some of their personal items, including essential medicines and other goods, by border authorities, despite these having been cleared during electronic and manual scanning and customs clearance.

Sources said that several such complaints had been lodged with both border and customs authorities for the return of confiscated items, but the verification process by the authorities was painfully slow, much to the disappointment of the returning families.

stories.title: Stakeholders agree on revival of Islamabad’s Covered Market in G-6
summary: The participants agreed that a ground-plus one storey would be allowed in the market. “Minutes of the final meeting are yet to be issued.

Last year, before seeking public opinion, the matter was placed before the CDA board and the planning wing in its summary surprisingly did not inform the board that the market was constructed by the CDA itself before leasing it out in 1966.

Sources said in the latest hearing it was stated that ground-plus one storey and lower ground and basement in parking should be allowed. “The matter will be presented before the CDA board for final approval,” said an officer of CDA.

stories.title: Karachi's JPMC gets endoscopic ultrasound facility
summary: The sophisticated equipment was donated by Getz Pharma following a request from JPMC’s gastroenterology department to the company to improve diagnostic services for underprivileged patients from Karachi, interior Sindh and Balochistan.

According to hospital officials, EUS-guided procedures, which can cost between Rs300,000 and Rs400,000 in the private sector, would now become accessible to patients free of charge who otherwise struggle to afford specialised investigations.
He expressed hope that the facility would reduce diagnostic delays, facilitate earlier treatment and improve outcomes for patients unable to afford expensive private-sector services.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Cantonment Board to launch three-day anti-beggary drive
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Rawalpindi Cantonment Board (RCB) has decided to launch a three-day anti-beggary awareness campaign from November 10 to 12, 2026, aimed at making the cantonment area free of beggars and raising civic awareness among residents.
As part of the awareness drive, the civic body is installing billboards, display skins and informational streamers along major roads, commercial centres and key intersections.
The RCB administration emphasised that eliminating beggary was not possible without active public cooperation.

stories.title: Drug supply in police vehicle: SHO among four cops suspended as NCF arrests constable in Faisalabad
summary: Official sources say that the NCF got a tip-off that the suspect, Constable Kashif, posted at Gulberg police station, Faisalabad, was bringing five kilogram hashish to hand it over to a local drug seller, using the SHO’s official vehicle.

RAPE SUSPECT HELD: A man allegedly involved in raping and harassing minor girls, and making their obscene videos, has been arrested on Saturday night in an injured condition following a police “encounter” in Faisalabad.

Police sources say Roshanwala police SHO Rai Shahid Mahmood, along with a team, raided a premises at Chak 224 RB, Waseeran, to arrest the suspect, Arif Hussain, who was facing allegations of raping and harassing minor girls, and making their obscene videos.

stories.title: Sahiwal by-poll runner-up booked for threatening officials
summary: SAHIWAL: Police registered a case against runner-up candidate Awais Mahmood and 26 supporters of his political party, Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan, on charges of issuing threats to election officials and disrupting polling during the by-election in PP-203, Chichawatni, the other day.
The case was lodged with Saddar Police Station, Chichawatni, on the complaint of Gulraiz Khan, presiding officer of polling station No 102, Govt Boys High School, Chak 102/12-L.

Both the DPO and the RO said the case had been registered on the basis of a written complaint submitted by the presiding officer, who exercised magistracy powers on polling day under the election laws.

stories.title: Hyderabad board declares mark sheets of 43 MDCAT-pass candidates ‘tampered’
summary: Officials said that the LUMHS had sent mark sheets of 48 candidates to BISE for verification on the orders of a division bench of the Sindh High Court on a petition filed by a girl student who secured 150 out of 180 marks in MDCAT.
Later, the director of admissions of LUMHS had sent a letter to the BISE controller of examinations, requesting him to urgently verify the credentials of 48 students.
Officials said that the BISE declared the transcripts of only five candidates authentic, while the mark sheets of the remaining 43 candidates were found to have been tampered with.

stories.title: Around 6,000 police personnel deployed on Test match security in Rawalpindi
summary: As many as 1,000 additional police personnel have been called to Rawalpindi from other districts to assist the local police in ensuring tight security arrangements for the cricket match.
The RPO clarified that foolproof security and excellent traffic arrangements were the top priorities during an international cricket match.
Effective traffic arrangements have been made for the convenience of citizens, while foolproof security and traffic arrangements were being ensured for the match.

stories.title: Better use of available water key to fixing Karachi supply: Murad
summary: The chief minister reviewed a series of measures to improve Karachi’s water supply by reducing losses in the canal system, enhancing water conveyance efficiency and strengthening the supply arrangements under the much-awaited K-IV project.

Reviewing the storage position of Keenjhar Lake and the feasibility of Kotri Barrage, the chief minister directed the relevant departments to ensure uninterrupted water supply to Karachi and Hyderabad during the forthcoming canal and barrage closure.

He further directed the authorities to closely monitor progress on the KB Feeder lining works and ensure that the anticipated water savings were properly assessed and factored into future supply planning for Karachi.

stories.title: Commercialisation of residential plot doesn’t permit construction without approval: SHC
summary: Permission for change of land use does not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of obtaining approval for construction, additions or alterations”.

The bench also said that the NOC for change of land use relied upon by the owner of the property cannot, without examination of its terms and the relevant building approvals, be treated as blanket authorisation for every structural alteration carried out at the premises.

Therefore, it directed the SBCA to perform its statutory functions and determine the legality of the construction on the basis of the relevant record, including the building plan, subsequent approvals, NOC for change of land use and any revised or amended plans.

stories.title: PML-N, PMML trade barbs over NA-77 by-election
summary: According to unofficial results, PML-N candidate Rashid Bashir Virk secured 43,365 votes in NA-77, defeating his rival, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League’s Ibrahim Gujjar, who bagged 30,218 votes.
On the other hand, the PMML rejected the NA-77 by-election results, alleging widespread rigging and violations of the election commission’s code of conduct.
Punjab Police were used for political campaigning in favour of the PML-N candidate and for pressuring voters,” Mr Nadeem alleged.

stories.title: Jamaat-i-Islami steps up mobilisation drive for Quetta rally
summary: QUETTA: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Balochistan chief Maulana Hidayatur Rehman, who represents Gwadar in the provincial assembly, has said a public gathering scheduled to be held in Quetta on Nov 15 would give fresh momentum to the struggle for the rights of the province.

Addressing the newly elected office-bearers of the party, the party’s provincial chief urged them to launch a door-to-door campaign through newly formed and energetic teams to ensure the success of the Nov 15 gathering.
Maulana Hidayatur Rehman pointed out that despite not being in government, the party continued to serve people in education, healthcare, welfare and the provision of basic facilities.

stories.title: Urea ban lifted in 17 more Balochistan districts
summary: QUETTA: The Balochistan government conditionally lifted the ban on the sale and purchase of urea fertiliser in 17 more districts on Monday evening, according to an official notification.
Agriculture Department officers, deputy commissioners and law enforcement agencies will strictly monitor fertiliser stocks and their movement, reporting any violations immediately.
Dealers found violating the prescribed procedures will face strict action and have their licences cancelled.

summary: In the first case, the NCCIA recovered Rs1.8m from suspects involved in an online investment fraud in which a citizen was defrauded of over Rs2.9m through Facebook and WhatsApp.
In the second case, the NCCIA recovered Rs1.4m in an online trading and investment fraud in which a Rawalpindi resident was defrauded of over Rs21m.

Officials said the NCCIA was committed to taking strict action against those involved in child exploitation, blackmailing, online fraud and fake investment schemes, adding that no one would be spared.

stories.title: Another Chaudhry slams Maryam over ‘development bias’
summary: The latest salvo was fired by PML-Q MNA Chaudhry Hussain Elahi, who echoed his cousin Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s criticism of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz over alleged corruption and a discriminatory approach in the allocation of development funds for various constituencies.

Speaking at a recent public gathering at Qila Islam Nagar near Tanda, Hussain Elahi accused the incumbent chief minister of blocking uplift funds for schemes launched during the tenure of former CM Chaudhry Parvez Elahi in 2022.

Speaking on the occasion, his father Chaudhry Wajahat Hussain — the younger brother of PML-Q chief Chaudhry Shujaat — also praised the tenure of Parvez Elahi, recalling the public welfare schemes launched under his stewardship.

stories.title: Starc denies knowledge of ball-tampering plot
summary: Fast bowler Mitchell Starc denied on Tuesday any prior knowledge of Australia's plot to tamper with the ball during the 2018 tour of South Africa, as Cricket Australia boss Todd Greenberg ruled out another investigation into 'Sandpapergate'.

Starc is the first of Australia's bowlers to respond to Usman Khawaja's assertions in his autobiography and on social media that the whole team knew of a plan ⁠to manipulate the ball in order to get it to reverse swing.
Starc said Khawaja's account was the first time he was aware of ball-tampering taking place in Gqeberha.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars appoint Aminul Islam as advisor
summary: Lahore Qalandars have appointed former Bangladesh captain Aminul Islam as an advisor to the franchise's High-Performance Centres, the Pakistan Super League side said on Tuesday.

The appointment is part of Lahore Qalandars' efforts to strengthen their grassroots cricket initiatives and expand their outreach in Bangladesh by drawing on Islam's experience in international cricket and administration.
During his playing days, Islam represented Bangladesh from 1988 to 2002 and captained the national side at the 1999 Cricket World Cup.

stories.title: Pochettino favored to be next Manchester United manager
summary: United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino is the top candidate to be the next Manchester United manager, ESPN reported ‌on Monday.
Manchester United reportedly are considering firing manager Michael Carrick after the squad has slipped to 18th in the Premier League table with a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on ⁠Sunday.

Per ESPN, Manchester United's hierarchy also are considering former ⁠Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe for the position, as well as former Ipswich Town coach Kieran McKenna and ⁠former German national team coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Voter anger over the war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, intensifying Republican divisions over a conflict that Vice President J.
Trump has backed Hegseth and condemned the impeachment push in an interview with CBS broadcast on Sunday. “They want to impeach him.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teen, wound 3 others in occupied West Bank
summary: Israeli soldiers in civilian clothes join attacks on Palestinians in West Bank: probe Israeli soldiers have joined armed groups of Israeli occupiers attacking Palestinians in the West Bank while wearing civilian clothes, an Al Jazeera investigation broadcast Monday found.

Israeli army raids and attacks by Israeli occupiers have intensified in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since October 2023, with reports of killings, arrests, home demolitions, arson attacks, the bulldozing of land and the displacement of Palestinian communities.
The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission recorded 1,369 attacks by Israeli occupiers in October.

stories.title: PSX roars back after long weekend, KSE-100 jumps 4,654 points
summary: Investors returned to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) with renewed enthusiasm on Tuesday after a long weekend, unleashing a strong buying spree that sent the benchmark KSE-100 index soaring as much as 4,654 points in morning trade.

The market, which remained closed on Monday for Iqbal Day, opened on a firm note, with the benchmark index climbing to 176,739.00 points by 9:34am, gaining 2,852.32 points, or 1.64%, from the previous close.
The index touched an intraday high of 178,606.21 points, while its low stood at 176,273.72 points.
